name: Raven CI
summary: A small CI/CD server whose core holds only the queue, the model of jobs and builds and the register of plugins; every function of a CI (pipeline formats, steps, git, providers, triggers, publishers, agents) is a plugin, compiled in or a program of any language over JSON-RPC.
when_to_use: To see which plugins Raven CI has, whether each is on, and why one was refused.
To switch a plugin on or off without restarting anything.
To check that the core and the API of plugins work on this machine (--self-test).
To ask a running server for a build, follow it and take its evidence from a terminal or an agent (rodar, status, log, resumo, evidencia, with --format json).
To install the server as a service of the system (servico instalar).

commands.does: Lists every plugin: version, origin (compiled in or external), state (on, off, or refused with the reason) and the points it offers.
Shows one plugin: dependencies with the versions accepted, permissions declared and granted, configuration and memory.
Switches the plugin on and says what else changed.
Switches the plugin off, with the plugins that need it, and says which.

Sobe o servidor: HTTP com login (GET /health aberto, /api/ci/jobs, /api/ci/build, /api/ci/log?after= e as rotas dos plugins), os executores e os gatilhos dos jobs. Diz o endereço na primeira linha e para com Ctrl+C ou SIGTERM.

commands.command: echo SENHA | raven-ci usuario criar NOME [--papel Executores|Leitores|Administradores]
commands.does: Cria quem pode entrar no servidor; o primeiro é administrador. A senha vem na primeira linha da entrada.

commands.command: raven-ci rodar JOB [--param NOME=VALOR]... [--prioridade N] [--esperar] [--servidor URL] [--format json]
commands.does: Pede um build ao servidor (POST /api/ci/run, com a chave em RAVEN_CI_TOKEN); com --esperar segue o log e sai com 0 só se passou.
O build no servidor (o último, sem número): estado, causa, quem pediu, duração, parâmetros, etapas e anexos.
O log do build; --seguir lê /api/ci/log?after= até o build acabar (em JSON, uma linha por linha do log).
Cada job do servidor com o último build e o estado, e quantos estão na fila.

commands.command: raven-ci evidencia JOB NUMERO PASTA [--format json]
commands.does: Baixa os artefatos do build (plugin artifacts) e o log.txt para PASTA.

Aplica a configuração como código (raven-ci.toml: jobs, pastas, plugins e a configuração deles, url) à pasta de dados ou, com --servidor, ao servidor no ar, que vigia de novo os gatilhos do que mudou; um job fora do arquivo só sai com --remover.
O servidor como serviço do sistema: systemd com MemoryMax, launchd no macOS ou tarefa do Agendador do Windows; estado sai com 0 só se roda.
Runs a subcommand a plugin brings, such as `raven-ci hello Ana` from the example plugin.
Puts a core together in memory with a fake plugin for every extension point and runs a build through all of them; exit code 0 when it passed.

options.does: The folder of its data (also RAVEN_CI_HOME); ~/.raven-ci by default. The external plugins are found in its plugins/ folder and in the folders given with --plugins.
Another folder of external plugins, one folder per plugin with its plugin.toml.

limits: It has no window and no HTTP server yet: the panel, the agents and the API come in the next phases of #803.
No plugin for real work ships yet (shell, git, GitHub, TOML pipelines): they are phase 2 of #803.
Switching a plugin on or off from the command line changes what the next start of the server loads; the core switches them live, with no restart, through its API.
The memory of a plugin compiled in is not measured apart from the server's; an external plugin's is, on Linux and macOS.
The memory limit of the service (servico instalar --memoria) is enforced only by systemd, on Linux; launchd and the Task Scheduler of Windows take no limit.
